newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rautaruukki says privatisation under way.
newsitem.headline: Rautaruukki says privatisation under way.

text.p: Finnish steel group Rautaruukki Oy said in a statement on Wednesday preparations for a further privatisation were under way and the Finnish state's ownership would fall below 50 percent from 68.7 percent now.
"In connection with a broadening of the ownership base, the state of Finland's stake in Rautaruukki would fall below 50 percent," it said, adding that no decisions had yet been made.
Rautaruukki also said steel products prices had started to strengthen in the first months of 1997 but that they would remain lower than in early 1996.

"Rautaruukki's first tertial earnings will therefore be as expected lower than in the the year-ago period, which was the best of last year's tertials," it said. "The company's 1997 earnings are estimated to be better than in 1996 provided the steel market develops as expected."

Rautaruukki said the ministry of trade and industry had in recent months studied ways of broadening Rautaruukki Oy's ownership base and has begun preparations to offer shares to domestic and foreign investors.
It said new shares could possibly be offered to institutional investors in connection with an offering of the government's shares.
The lead managers for the planned offering are SBC Warburg and Union Bank of Switzerland, with Merita Corporate Finance as domestic lead manager, Rautaruukki said.
